cim: Curators approve Missouri S&T to offer state’s first bachelor’s degree in AI
cim_eredeti: Curators approve Missouri S&T to offer state’s first bachelor’s degree in AI
szoveg_eredeti:
Eliot Kimmel, a Ph.D. student in computer science, walks Joe Joe around the Missouri S&T campus. Joe Joe is a humanoid robot that often attends events and greets visitors to the university. Photo by Blaine Falkena/Missouri S&T

The University of Missouri Board of Curators voted unanimously today (Thursday, Nov. 19) to approve a new bachelor’s degree program in artificial intelligence (AI) at Missouri S&T. When the program is launched in fall 2027, the degree will be the first standalone undergraduate AI degree offered in Missouri.

“Demand for AI-focused education has grown significantly as AI technologies become increasingly integrated into industries ranging from manufacturing and transportation to healthcare and financial services,” says Dr. David Borrok, vice provost and dean of the College of Engineering and Computing at S&T. “Our graduates will be prepared to understand and innovate within modern engineered systems that are increasingly using AI.”

The degree will be housed in Missouri S&T’s computer science department within the College of Engineering and Computing. It will combine computer science fundamentals, mathematics, data science and ethics with specialized coursework and hands-on learning experiences in artificial intelligence. The program will require 120 credit hours. The program’s focus extends beyond a traditional computer science degree with an AI emphasis by providing comprehensive preparation in both the theory and practice of artificial intelligence.

The degree aligns with Missouri’s workforce development priorities, including Missouri Executive Order 26-02, which directs the state’s higher education and workforce agencies to support the development of AI-focused degree programs. The proposal also supports Missouri S&T’s strategic goals related to enrollment growth, academic innovation and workforce preparation.

Students will study core topics including programming, algorithms, machine learning, data science, computer organization, databases and cybersecurity. The curriculum also includes coursework in calculus, linear algebra, statistics and neuroscience, along with a focus on responsible AI practices and the societal effects of emerging technologies.

“Experiential learning will be a key component of this program,” says Dr. Seung-Jong Jay Park, S&T’s Kummer Endowed Chair of Computer Science. “Students will complete project-based coursework and participate in a senior capstone experience that may be sponsored by industry, government laboratories or university researchers.”

The proposal includes six new courses developed specifically for the degree program: Introduction to Modern AI Tools, Introduction to Artificial Intelligence, Introduction to Machine Learning, Intelligent Robots, Responsible AI and Computing, and an AI Capstone course.

Graduates will prepare for careers such as AI application developer, machine learning engineer, data scientist, intelligent systems developer, AI solutions analyst and AI-enabled cybersecurity analyst.

Missouri S&T projects enrollment of approximately 110 students within five years of the program’s launch. The next step in the approval process will be for the Missouri Coordinating Board for Higher Education to review S&T’s proposal. Pending CBHE approval, the university aims to admit students into this new major starting in fall 2027.
